# BucketDB

TypeScript document database (version 0.6.0). Uses AWS S3 / Alibaba Cloud OSS / local filesystem / memory as backend. No database server, no runtime dependencies. Requires Node >= 22 or Bun. Includes the `bucket-db` CLI.

## Key concepts

- `BucketDB` — `BucketDB.connect(url?, { logger? })` (url default: env BUCKET_DB_URL) or `new BucketDB(adapter, dbPath, { logger? })`; `dbPath` is a key prefix (`''` = bucket root, may contain `/`)
- Connection URLs: `s3://bucket/prefix?region=&endpoint=&forcePathStyle=&timeoutMs=`, `oss://bucket/prefix?region=&endpoint=&timeoutMs=`, `file:///abs/dir` or `file://./rel/dir` (dbPath ''), `memory://prefix`. Path = dbPath. Unknown query parameters → ValidationError. Credentials never in the URL (`user:secret@` is refused); they come from env (AWS_* / OSS_* / ALIBABA_CLOUD_*). Error messages never repeat the URL, so it is safe to log. URL-encode `endpoint` values.
- `Collection<T>` — typed collection, returned by `db.collection<T>(name)` (same instance per name). Exported as a type only: there is no `new Collection(...)` and no `CollectionOptions` (0.6); set the logger on BucketDB.
- Storage: one JSON object per document at `<dbPath>/<collection>/docs/<id>.json`. No index, no log, no result cache. Format unchanged since 0.4.
- Query snapshot (S3 / OSS / custom adapters with `remote: true` only): `<dbPath>/<collection>/_snapshot.v1.json` = `{ format: 'bucket-db-snapshot', version: 1, documents: { <id>: { etag, body } } }`. find LISTs docs/, uses a snapshot entry only if its etag equals the listed etag, GETs the rest (16 in parallel). The LIST is the authority: a missing/corrupt/stale/overwritten snapshot only costs speed, never changes results. Rewritten (unconditional PUT) when > 16 documents had to be read individually (+ entries of deleted docs). Memory / FileSystem keep no snapshot.
- Every document extends `Document`: `id` (generated UUID unless chosen, taken from the object key), `_etag` (from storage, not stored in the body), `_createdAt`, `_updatedAt`
- Returned documents are `Stored<T>` = `T & { _etag: string }`: `_etag` always set (no `!` needed); `_createdAt` / `_updatedAt` stay optional (hand-placed files may lack them)
- `InsertDocument<T>` and `UpdateDocument<T>` exclude `id`, `_etag`, `_createdAt`, `_updatedAt` (UpdateDocument is also Partial); system fields passed at runtime are dropped
- put vs insert: `put(id, data)` creates or replaces the whole document (unconditional, idempotent, resets `_createdAt`); `insert(data, { id })` creates only if the id is free, else DocumentExistsError; `insert(data)` generates a UUID.
- Optimistic locking: `update(id, data, { etag: doc._etag })`; stale etag or lost race throws ConcurrentUpdateError (no retry). Works on Memory, S3, and FileSystem within one process. On OSS, update with etag throws UnsupportedError.
- update without etag: on Memory / FileSystem (one process) / S3, conflicting writes are retried (up to 5 retries) so concurrent partial updates all apply; on OSS last writer wins. update keeps `_createdAt`.

## Guarantees per backend

|                                      | Memory | FileSystem             | S3  | OSS                              |
|--------------------------------------|--------|------------------------|-----|----------------------------------|
| single write atomic                  | yes    | yes                    | yes | yes                              |
| create-if-absent (insert, also { id })| yes   | yes (across processes) | yes | yes (non-versioned buckets only) |
| conditional update (etag)            | yes    | single process only    | yes | no — UnsupportedError            |
| concurrent partial updates all apply | yes    | single process         | yes | no (last writer wins)            |

Multiple writer processes are supported for insert/put/delete on every backend and for update on S3 (Memory/FileSystem: within one process). put is last-writer-wins everywhere.

## Limitations (0.6.0)

- No transactions; each write touches one document. deleteMany is not atomic (one DELETE per match, 16 in parallel; a failure leaves earlier deletes done).
- Envelope: at most 10,000 documents and 10 MB of snapshot per collection; past it the collection logs one `warn` and queries keep getting slower. Measured warm find at 10,000 docs: OSS 1.35 s, S3 3.2 s, FileSystem ~0.5 s; no snapshot at 10,000 docs: OSS 34 s, S3 134 s (docs/BENCHMARKS.md).
- find cost on S3/OSS: ⌈N/1000⌉ LIST + 1 GET (snapshot) + 1 GET per document changed since the snapshot (≤ 16), or those GETs + 1 snapshot PUT when more changed. Memory/FileSystem: ⌈N/1000⌉ LIST + N GET. `{ id: '...' }` reads one document. sort/limit/offset do not reduce reads. count() without filter: LIST only.
- Results are not a point-in-time snapshot: each returned document is some committed version.
- Snapshot read errors other than not-found (transient, permission) fail find with StorageError. Snapshot write failures do not fail find; they go to the logger (level `error`); after 401/403 (read-only credentials) the collection stops writing it.
- Deleted documents' contents remain in the snapshot until it is rewritten or `compact()` runs.
- OSS: no conditional update (etag → UnsupportedError); concurrent etag-less updates are last-writer-wins.
- FileSystem: etag checks / concurrent update merging hold only within one process.
- 0.3.x and 0.4+ clients must not write the same collection concurrently. 0.4+ reads 0.3 data as-is; it reads only `docs/` and `_snapshot.v1.json` and skips 0.3's `*.meta` files, so 0.3's index and log directories can be deleted. 0.4, 0.5 and 0.6 share the format.
- Proxies: the S3/OSS client uses the runtime's built-in fetch. Bun (1.4.2) honours HTTPS_PROXY by default. Node (22.23.5, 24.22.3) ignores HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY by default and connects directly; set NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 (Node 22.21.0+ / 24.0.0+) or `--use-env-proxy` (22.21.0+ / 24.5.0+; Node marks it Stability 1.1, active development), e.g. `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy:3128 npx -y @hold-baby/bucket-db count items`. NO_PROXY is honoured on both (exact host, domain suffix with or without leading dot, `*`).

## Package: @hold-baby/bucket-db

### Exports

Classes: BucketDB, MemoryStorageAdapter, FileSystemAdapter, S3Adapter, OSSAdapter
Errors: BucketDBError, ValidationError, DocumentNotFoundError, DocumentExistsError, ConcurrentUpdateError, UnsupportedError, StorageError
Types: Collection (type only), BucketDBOptions, Logger, LogEvent, Document, Stored, InsertDocument, UpdateDocument, QueryOperator, QueryValue, QueryFilter, QueryOptions, SortSpec, InsertOptions, UpdateOptions, FileSystemAdapterConfig, S3AdapterOptions, OSSAdapterOptions, Credentials, CredentialProvider, StorageAdapter, Capabilities, Guarantee, WriteCondition, ObjectEntry, ListPage, ListOptions, StorageErrorKind, StorageErrorOptions

### BucketDB API

```
BucketDB.connect(url?: string, options?: BucketDBOptions): BucketDB    // sync; url default process.env.BUCKET_DB_URL
new BucketDB(adapter: StorageAdapter, dbPath: string, options?: BucketDBOptions)
db.collection<T extends Document>(name: string): Collection<T>
```

### Collection API

```
insert(data: InsertDocument<T>, options?: InsertOptions): Promise<Stored<T>>  // 1 conditional PUT; generated UUID, or options.id (DocumentExistsError if taken)
put(id: string, data: InsertDocument<T>): Promise<Stored<T>>        // 1 unconditional PUT; create or replace whole doc; idempotent; resets _createdAt
findById(id: string): Promise<Stored<T> | null>                     // 1 GET; null ONLY if missing, other storage errors throw
find(filter?: QueryFilter<T>, options?: QueryOptions<T>): Promise<Stored<T>[]>   // LIST + snapshot (S3/OSS) or GET all (local); default order _createdAt then id
count(filter?: QueryFilter<T>): Promise<number>             // no filter: LIST only; with filter: like find
update(id: string, data: UpdateDocument<T>, options?: UpdateOptions): Promise<Stored<T>>   // GET + conditional PUT
delete(id: string): Promise<void>                           // 1 DELETE; no error if missing
deleteMany(filter: QueryFilter<T>): Promise<number>         // find + 1 DELETE per match (16 parallel); NOT atomic; returns count
compact(): Promise<void>                                    // S3/OSS: rebuild the snapshot (LIST + GET all + PUT), drops deleted docs' contents; throws on failure; no-op locally
```

### Logger

```
BucketDB.connect(url, { logger: (event: LogEvent) => void })   // or new BucketDB(adapter, dbPath, { logger }); default: console.warn
LogEvent = { level: 'warn' | 'error', message: string, error?: unknown }
```

Receives: snapshot write failures (error), unparsable snapshot being rebuilt (warn), envelope exceeded (warn, once per collection).

### QueryOptions<T> / InsertOptions / UpdateOptions

```
{ sort?: SortSpec<T>, limit?: number, offset?: number }   // filter → sort → offset/limit, in memory
SortSpec<T> = Partial<Record<keyof T | 'id' | '_etag' | '_createdAt' | '_updatedAt', 1 | -1>>   // unknown sort field = compile error; a field set to undefined is ignored
{ id?: string }
{ etag?: string }
```

Order: default `_createdAt` asc then `id` asc (stable pagination); with sort, ties fall back to `_createdAt`, `id`. Missing/null values sort last in either direction. Mixed types: booleans < numbers < strings < others (JSON text). `limit: 0` → []. Negative/fractional limit/offset, sort direction not 1/-1 (undefined is ignored), reserved sort field → ValidationError before any request.

### Query operators

$eq, $ne, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in, $nin (fields and operators combined with AND).
Semantics (settled in 0.5): a missing field is `undefined`. Missing field: $eq / plain value / ranges / $in → no match; $ne / $nin → match. Range operators only compare number-number or string-string; any other combination (mismatched types, booleans, null, objects) is no match, never an error. Equality is strict ===. `$in: []` matches nothing; `$nin: []` excludes nothing. `{ f: null }` does not match a missing f; `{ f: { $ne: null } }` does. No $exists.
Unknown operators, non-array $in/$nin, reserved field names (constructor, __proto__, …) throw ValidationError before any request.

### Adapters

```
new MemoryStorageAdapter()
new FileSystemAdapter({ basePath })
new S3Adapter({ bucket, region?, endpoint?, credentials?, forcePathStyle?, timeoutMs? })
new OSSAdapter({ bucket, region?, endpoint?, credentials?, timeoutMs? })
credentials: { accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken?, expiresAt? } | (() => Promise<that>)   // provider re-called 5 min before expiresAt
```

Custom adapters implement StorageAdapter { capabilities, remote?, get, put, delete, list }; set `remote: true` to get the query snapshot (S3Adapter and OSSAdapter do). insert with { id } needs capabilities.createIfAbsent !== 'none' (else UnsupportedError).

S3 defaults: region AWS_REGION / AWS_DEFAULT_REGION; endpoint AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3 / AWS_ENDPOINT_URL / https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com; credentials AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_SESSION_TOKEN. Any S3-compatible service via endpoint; only AWS S3 and OSS are tested.
OSS defaults: region OSS_REGION (`cn-hangzhou`; `oss-cn-hangzhou` also accepted); endpoint https://s3.oss-<region>.aliyuncs.com (S3-compatible; OSS_ENDPOINT is not read); credentials OSS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / OSS_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET / OSS_SESSION_TOKEN, else ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID / ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET / ALIBABA_CLOUD_SECURITY_TOKEN (aliyun/configure-aliyun-credentials-action).
Path-style addressing is automatic when the endpoint host is localhost or an IP address (IPv4, or IPv6 like `[::1]`); forcePathStyle overrides it.
Retries (S3 and OSS): up to 3 attempts, per-attempt timeout 10 s (timeoutMs), on network errors, timeouts, 5xx, 429, SlowDown, RequestTimeout.

### Error mapping

ValidationError        — invalid collection name / document ID / dbPath segment / filter / sort / limit / offset; missing or invalid connection URL (unknown scheme or parameter, no bucket, credentials in URL); invalid adapter options; missing credentials
DocumentNotFoundError  — update on a missing doc
DocumentExistsError    — insert with an id that is taken
ConcurrentUpdateError  — update with stale etag, lost race with etag, or etag-less update retries exhausted
UnsupportedError       — backend lacks the capability (OSS update with etag)
StorageError           — storage failure; fields kind ('not-found' | 'conflict' | 'transient' | 'permanent'), key, status. Also thrown by find for a file under docs/ that is not `<id>.json` holding a JSON object (key names the file). Hidden files (starting with `.`) are ignored.
All extend BucketDBError.

Names: collection names, document IDs and each `/`-separated dbPath segment must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,255}$ and not start with `.`; otherwise ValidationError (never rewritten).

## CLI: bucket-db

```
npx @hold-baby/bucket-db <command> [arguments] [--url <url>]     # URL from --url or BUCKET_DB_URL
get <collection> <id>                     # print document; exit 2 if missing
put <collection> <id> [json]              # create or replace; JSON from argument or stdin
find <collection> [filter] [--sort field[:asc|:desc]]... [--limit n] [--offset n]   # prints one JSON array
count <collection> [filter]               # prints a number
delete <collection> <id>                  # no error if missing
export <collection>                       # JSON Lines, no _etag
import <collection> [file]                # JSON Lines from file/stdin; lines with id written in storage format (keeps id + timestamps, overwrites); lines without id inserted; prints count
compact <collection>                      # rebuild snapshot
doctor                                    # check backend guarantees; writes only under <prefix>/_doctor-<time>/, cleans up
```

stdout: one JSON value per line (jq-friendly); errors on stderr prefixed `bucket-db: `. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error (incl. a failed doctor check), 2 not found (get). Filters are JSON objects: `'{"ms":{"$lt":100}}'`.
doctor checks: object round trip; LIST reflects writes/overwrites/deletes immediately with matching etags; create-if-absent with 10 concurrent writers (exactly one wins); compare-and-swap with 10 concurrent writers (skipped where declared none, e.g. OSS). Lines start with `ok`, `skip` or `FAIL`; last line `all checks passed` or `<n> check(s) failed`.
CI: key records by run (`put runs "$GITHUB_RUN_ID-<shard>"`) so re-runs overwrite; per-job OIDC credentials (AWS_* / ALIBABA_CLOUD_*); recipes in examples/ci/ of the repository.
